title: Field Ask Batch Mapper & Implementation Level-of-Detail Guide
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable mapper that ingests batches of Sales/CS enterprise feature asks and assigns an initial Implementation Level-of-Detail (LOD) + first-pass engineering sizing. The outcome will be a short, consistent brief per account bundle that PM/ENG/Design can use to decide next steps (quick-win, discovery spike, or scoped epic). Focus on non-bug feature asks and avoid duplicating existing intake playbooks — this prioritizes batch normalization, LOD heuristics, and predictable handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: A batch intake template (CSV + UI checklist) that Sales/CS can use to submit grouped asks
An LOD rubric (LOD1/LOD2/LOD3) with corresponding deliverables and estimated point ranges
A mapping script or spreadsheet that translates intake signals into recommended LOD and an initial cost band
Two trial batches processed with AE/SE participants and documented outcomes
Handoff checklist that provides required artifacts for engineering discovery on LOD2/LOD3 items
steps: Interview 6 AEs & 3 Solutions Engineers to capture common ask shapes and the minimum info they can provide
Define LOD taxonomy and attach example archetypes (prefix-routing, dedicated capacity requests, private deployment compliance asks)
Build a lightweight intake template (CSV + short Airtable / Google Sheet) for batch uploads
Create scoring heuristics: account ARR, ask breadth, security/regulatory surface, implementation surface area, ROI proxy
Run two pilot batches (Sales West, CS Onboarding) and collect feedback
Refine rubric, write handoff checklist, and add to Sales/CS playbook
notes: We must keep the template intentionally low-friction — aim for <10 fields per ask when possible
Map common technical signals to Redwood product areas: runtime (batching, KV cache), Dedicated capacity, Private/VPC, Console UX
Initial cost bands should be presented as story point ranges (LOD1: 1-5, LOD2: 6-20, LOD3: 21+)
Escalation path: high-security requests auto-escalate to Security & Compliance for review
For enterprise asks that mention SLA/SLA-tier changes, add 'ops-impact' flag so we consult Reliability early
comments: 2026-03-11: Discovery call with AE team (lead: Mark Johnson). Observed AEs can provide priority, use-case summary, and rough ARR estimate but rarely technical constraints.
2026-03-12: SE feedback (Lina Chen): need a checkbox for 'requires dedicated capacity' and a short field for 'expected throughput' — added to template draft.
2026-03-13: PM review (Aisha): recommend adding a short 'customer risk' signal (regulatory/data residency). Diego to incorporate in scoring.
2026-03-14: Engineering sync (Diego, Priya Rao): suggested mapping of LOD2 to 'technical spike' with explicit acceptance criteria and proposed 2-week spike default for unknowns.
2026-03-15: Pilot batch scheduling confirmed for 2026-03-22 with Sales-West and CS-Onboarding reps. Sessions framed as 30-minute rapid scoping workshops.
implementation_examples: Example A (LOD1): Customer asks for a Console dashboard tweak to show per-route token cost. Deliverable: product spec + small frontend PR. Estimate 3 pts.

Example B (LOD2): Large account requests Dedicated capacity with custom autoscale policy. Deliverable: discovery spike to enumerate infra constraints and design HA plan. Estimate 8-15 pts depending on blockers.
Example C (LOD3): On-prem Private deployment with HSM integration and audit logs. Deliverable: multi-sprint epic with security review, architect design, and infra changes. Estimate 40+ pts.
handoff_checklist: Customer summary (1 page): need, value metric, urgency
Account signals: ARR band, support tier, compliance requirements
Ask artifacts: screenshots, example prompt/workload, expected throughput
Suggested LOD and initial point band
Suggested next owner and timeline (e.g., schedule 2-week discovery)
risks: If intake requires too many fields adoption will be low
Overly broad bundles can mask independent low-effort wins — enforce per-ask minimum description
Underestimating security/ops impact on Dedicated/Private requests could derail estimates
